title: Weekly Market Review
text:
BOTTOM LINE — Risk-on bounce; semis and miners led, energy lagged badly. The week’s arc was a sharp rebound from August 6’s record-high pullback, with tech and gold/silver absorbing flows while oil’s spike faded. Dominant driver was a dovish rate narrative plus strong earnings, though breadth stayed narrow under the surface.

INDICES — QQQ +5.09%, SPY +3.51%, IWM +3.56%, DIA +2.92%; large beat small by 1.53pp. VIX fell to 14.9, below its 20-day of 17.2. Most notable cross-asset move: SLV +9.82% WTD, gold GLD +7.25%. No index below its 200-day MA.

SECTORS & ROTATION — XLK +7.20%, XLB +4.82%, XLY +3.25%, XLI +2.97%, XLC +2.78%, XLV +1.93%, XLF +1.16%, XLP +0.08%, XLRE -0.20%, XLU -1.67%, XLE -3.44%. Top Industries: GDX +21.31%, SILJ +20.96%; bottom: XOP -6.20%, USO -8.66%. Money rotated into semis and precious metals, out of energy and defensives; state: AI hardware leading.

DRIVERS — Semis rebounded hard, SOXX +7.60% WTD, with XLK pacing sectors; silver and gold absorbed safe-haven flows as SLV +9.82% and GLD +7.25% outperformed. Energy was the clear laggard, XLE -3.44%, with USO -8.66% WTD despite Thursday’s oil spike on Hormuz headlines. Rate-sensitive macro stayed dovish per Fed’s Paulson comments; VIX compressed to 14.9 even as VXN at 22.8 shows tech-specific risk. Volume breadth was defensive—GLD 2.0x and SLV 1.5x average volume, while QQQ at 0.8x and SOXX 0.5x signaled participation was thin in the leaders.

WHAT'S NEXT — Watch whether the semi rally sustains on volume—SOXX at 0.5x volume suggests conviction is missing, and GDX’s 2.5x spike plus 21.31% WTD looks overextended for mean reversion. VIX 14.9 with SPY ATM_IV at 8.5% screams complacency; a break of the 770 GEX flip could trigger forced buying. Energy’s -3.44% WTD divergence from oil’s 20d +8.54% sets up either a catch-up or a breakdown—monitor XLE vs USO into next week.
